results.title: Mastering L2 Regularization: Stability, Smoothness, and Shrinkage
results.content: Instead of eliminating features, L2 smoothly shrinks all weights, preserving all predictors but keeping them small. L2 regularization, often referred to as Ridge regression in the context of linear models, adds a penalty to the loss function that is proportional to the sum of the squares of the weights. The unique characteristic of L2 regularization, instead of driving weights to zero (as in L1), L2 penalizes large weights, leading to smaller but non-zero values, which results in less sensitivity to individual data points and variance without adding much bias. Where L1 regularization encourages sparse models by eliminating irrelevant features, L2 regularization spreads the penalty across all coefficients. In practice, this means that L1 regularization can lead to simpler models that focus only on the most important features, discarding noise and irrelevant variables along the way. * Promotes Generalization: By discouraging large weights, L2 helps models generalize better to unseen data, reducing overfitting. * Handles Multicollinearity Well: When features are highly correlated, L2 distributes the weight more evenly instead of arbitrarily favoring or zeroing out some features. * Genomics and Bioinformatics: In gene expression modelling, L2 helps manage thousands of correlated features without eliminating potentially important genes. * Time-Series Forecasting: In ARIMA or regression-based models, L2 helps in regularizing lag features when many lags are introduced. * ElasticNet (sklearn.linear\_model.ElasticNet): Combines L1 + L2 regularization. * No Feature Selection: Unlike L1, L2 regularization does not zero out coefficients, so it doesn’t perform automatic feature selection. * Not Robust to Outliers: While generally more stable than L1, L2 regularization can still be influenced by extreme outliers affecting model coefficients. * Multicollinearity Handling: Although better than L1, L2 can still distribute weight across correlated features, which might dilute interpretability. L2 regularization is a reliable technique for building stable, generalizable, and smooth machine learning models. If you want a model that handles multicollinearity gracefully and prioritizes stability over sparsity, L2 regularization should be your go-to. * Mastering L1 Regularization: The Key to Simpler, Smarter Models. ### Mastering L1 Regularization: The Key to Simpler, Smarter Models.
